title: MHRN semantic prototype consolidation on Split-MNIST catastrophic forgetting
research_question: Does MHRN semantic prototype consolidation with bounded replay reduce catastrophic forgetting on class-incremental Split-MNIST relative to the same spike-coded online learner without semantic memory?
mechanism_under_test: SemanticMemory prototype consolidation plus bounded replay of mature prototypes

conditions.baseline: deterministic pooled rate-code spike representation plus online softmax readout; no semantic memory and no replay
conditions.semantic_replay: same representation, readout, seed and total readout-update budget; 20% of later-task updates are replaced by replay of mature MHRN semantic prototypes from earlier tasks

matched_controls: same total readout updates per task

primary_endpoints.final_average_accuracy: mean accuracy over all five tasks after training task 5
primary_endpoints.mean_forgetting: mean over tasks 1-4 of best historical accuracy minus final accuracy

statistical_rule: paired bootstrap 95% confidence interval and two-sided exact paired sign-flip test
positive_result_rule: semantic_replay must improve final average accuracy by at least 0.03 and reduce mean forgetting by at least 0.05; for both paired deltas the bootstrap 95% lower bound must exceed zero and sign-flip p must be below 0.05

interpretation.positive: bounded positive evidence that this MHRN mechanism improves this benchmark under this protocol; not proof of general superiority or biological validity
interpretation.null: infrastructure result or insufficient evidence under this protocol
interpretation.negative: the mechanism harms at least one primary endpoint under this protocol and is scientifically informative
